Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screen-less fitness tracker, similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who has been using WHOOP for six months, I agree the concept is good, but there are a few things I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in a relatively early stage of development, we don't yet know exactly what Apple's screen-less fitness tracker will look like. The earliest it could arrive is 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a thin fabric band with a sensor-laden computing module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase for a promotion where Sapphire cardholders could get a WHOOP at a discount or for free, and I took advantage of that. Since then, I've been using WHOOP, but I have never fully committed to it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection is never perfect, and I find that whether before or after a workout, having to pull out my phone to log it is really annoying. With an Apple Watch, you can start tracking directly from the watch face, and the data can sync back to WHOOP via Apple Health. That's the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

Going to the gym, pulling out your phone to operate it might still be acceptable; but for a leisurely bike ride or a long walk, I don't want to bother with taking out my phone.

So, for Apple's screen-less fitness tracker, I really hope to see physical buttons and indicator lights that can be used to start and stop workout tracking. After the fact, you'll of course still need to go back to your phone to categorise the workout, but I'd rather do that than have to deal with these things during exercise. Apple could also consider developing a classification model based on various factors.

Conclusion

If Apple can successfully develop a screen-less fitness tracker that doesn't feel like a hassle even without using your phone, I think it would be very appealing. This kind of design has many advantages, such as being more comfortable to wear, having longer battery life, and being able to be worn alongside a traditional watch.

Hot comments posted by TB

I bought a Fitbit Air because I've been wearing an Apple Watch almost exclusively for several years and started to feel a bit tired of it. I like mechanical watches, but I also want to keep tracking my health data and enjoy the convenience of a watch without having to take out my phone all the time (like quickly using Apple Pay, unlocking doors when my hands are tired, etc.). If Apple releases a product that fully integrates into the ecosystem, allowing me to use a streamlined version of Apple Pay, door keys, car keys, and other NFC functions, and can connect to AirPods to have Siri read my notifications or perform various tasks on my behalf, I would buy it immediately.

Speaking for myself, after trying WHOOP, I feel that I still prefer using a regular smartwatch, even if the battery life is insufficient. I understand some people might want a screen-less design so they won't be distracted, but for me, I just need to turn on Do Not Disturb mode on my watch and that's solved.

What do you think about Apple developing a screen-less fitness tracker? At what price would you buy one? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
